brief: UBS examines BIS's new rule restricting remote cloud access to advanced chips, which it says effectively revives Biden's unenacted AI Diffusion Rule and was unusually drafted at Treasury's direction. UBS cannot confirm the rule targets NVDA directly but calls the timing coincidental, consistent with risk it flagged in estimate cuts a day earlier. Chain: current law requires no license for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia or Singapore, so Malaysia's data-center build surged (2GW online, 10GW under construction, 25GW approved, backed by both US and China hyperscalers), with roughly half reportedly serving China-domiciled firms. A carve-out exists for retailers/social media, but US firms will likely compliance conservatively anyway, so UBS estimates 1-2GW of demand (mostly NVDA's) could be stripped, about 10% impact at $30B/GW; NVDA can divert shipments near-term, making this more a longer-term risk, especially if US power/shell permitting tightens. Separately, MATCH Act passage odds have risen (possible NDAA rider), though an expert argues the ASML/TEL-vs-US China sales gap is too small to justify it, a DUV ban risks trailing-edge China spillover, and FDPR use could upset allies more than tariffs. ASML/Japan suppliers are most exposed; KLAC is UBS's only indirectly-hit name via litho attach. Read-across: NVDA most directly hit; the memory-through-equipment chain suffers from the lost demand, though MATCH Act passage could eventually help non-China memory suppliers by capping China's domestic capacity.
